assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent=yes, daemon=full, driver=ready.

## agent = yes

Copilot CLI 1.0.77 ships a full in-REPL slash-command table (the TUI footer draws the `/ commands` hint the driver's `wait_ready` already greps for). The bundle carries the JS command definitions verbatim; `/usage` is the cleanest no-LLM member:

```js
{name:Jpe, help:"Display session usage metrics and statistics", allowDuringAgentExecution:!0,
 execute: async (t,e) => ({kind:"add-timeline-entry", entry:{type:"info", text: await t.session.usageOutput(), preserveAnsi:!0}})}
```

(`app.js` offset ~1668868.) It renders plan + AI-credit figures locally and returns a UI action — there is no model call anywhere on the path.

## daemon = full — the slash command writes NOTHING to events.jsonl

The question this cell turns on is which class a slash command falls in: Copilot has TWO emit paths, and only one reaches the transcript.

1. **The writer.** `events.jsonl` is written by the SessionEventWriter (`app.js` ~2533038): it subscribes `session.on("*")` and hands each event to a native `recordEventJson`. `emitInternal` (~2253182) is the single funnel: `u.ephemeral ? … : sessionRecordEventJson(u)` — non-ephemeral events are recorded, ephemeral ones are dispatched to listeners only. That is the documented split behind `session.todos_changed` / `user_input.requested` (both `emitEphemeral`) never appearing in the file while `tool.execution_start` / `permission.requested` (both `emit`) do.
2. **The slash dispatcher never reaches either path.** The TUI's submit handler (`app.js` ~7800573) tests the input for a command name, looks it up, `await Je.execute(Et, args)` and returns `{handled:!0}`. The prompt path — the ONLY code in the bundle that calls `.emit("user.message", …)` (6 sites, all inside `sendPrompt`-shaped functions) — is never entered. So a slash command is not logged as a user turn, and no `assistant.turn_start` / `assistant.turn_end` bracket is opened.
3. **`add-timeline-entry` is UI-only.** The action is applied as `u(Nt.entry)`; `u` is `addEntryToSession` in `Qfn`'s destructure (~7789567), and the call site (~8634781) passes `addEntryToSession: mi`, where `mi` is `addEphemeralEntry` from the React timeline hook (`{timeline:Ng, addEphemeralEntry:mi, …}`, ~8516764). It is in-memory React state. There is no "timeline" event type in the session vocabulary at all: enumerating every `.emit("…")` / `.emitEphemeral("…")` literal in the bundle yields ~60 persisted and ~48 ephemeral types, none of which a local render produces.
4. **`getSessionUsageOutput` is a pure read** (~8634943): it lists session dirs, reads their event logs (≤500, last 180d) and a quota snapshot to build the text. It emits nothing.

So the daemon's Source sees a transcript that does not grow during the slash window: no new line → no `transcript_activity` → the classifier has nothing to act on and the session stays `ready`. This is the codex shape (a slash that appends zero rollout lines), NOT the claudecode shape (a `<local-command>` wrapper the parser must filter) and NOT the aider shape (the slash logged as a real `####` user prompt, which flickers working).

Belt and braces: even if a lifecycle line DID land in the window — the periodic `session.usage_checkpoint` from `emitSessionLimitsUsageCheckpointIfNeeded` (~2313202) is the only realistic candidate — `parser.go` maps it through `parseUsage`, which sets `ev.Skip = true` (parser.go:301). Every event type other than `user.message` and `assistant.turn_end` is Skip or a non-state event kind, so nothing a local slash could plausibly trigger can move state. The user-observable assertion (`ready` throughout, no `→ working` for the slash itself, zero tool calls, no `waiting`) is exactly what this adapter produces.

## driver = ready

`replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` implements `slash` as a first-class arm (`slash_cmd`), and — critically — deliberately does NOT bump `EXPECTED_TURNS`, because a local render writes no `assistant.turn_end` and a bumped counter would hang the next `wait_turn` until timeout. `DRIVE_ELICITS` lists `send slash sleep wait_turn …`, and `DRIVE_SLASH_REQUIRES_STEP_TYPE=false` (copilot is a TUI, not headless-first). `/usage` takes no argument and opens no picker, so this is not a `keys` gap.

## Why the warm-up turn is mandatory

Copilot creates `session-state/<id>/` at launch holding only `workspace.yaml`, and writes `events.jsonl` only when the first prompt lands. Without a warm-up turn there is no real session at all — only the transient `proc-<PID>` row from the process scanner — and the cell would assert nothing about copilot's own session. The recipe therefore mirrors claudecode/codex: one cheap real turn, then the slash, then a settle sleep. The birth is modelled as the two-phase presession shape (`proc-<PID>` → real `<session-id>`), as for every other copilot cell.

## Command choice

`/usage` over the alternatives: `/clear` and `/new` both call `clearHistory` and rotate the session id (`app.js` ~1625923/~1626175 — `ykt` and `bkt`), which is the session-reset scenario; `/compact` is a real model call; a bare `/model` opens a picker dialog (a `show-dialog` action) that would need a `keys` step to dismiss. `/usage` is the only verified command that renders inline, takes no argument, and leaves the REPL in its normal state.
caveats: PROVISIONAL on emission, per the assess rule: daemon=full is derived from reading the CLI bundle and the adapter parser, not from a live capture of a driven /usage. The claim that events.jsonl does not grow during the slash window is a claim about what the AGENT writes; only the recording can settle it. If a future 1.0.x starts persisting a slash invocation (e.g. as a system.message), the parser still Skips it and state still cannot move — but the transcript-activity assertion in the verify block would need revisiting.

The two-phase presession birth carries the same provisional flag as the copilot basic-turn cell: it is derived from code reading (the 1s process-scanner poll mints proc-<PID> before events.jsonl exists), not from a captured birth. record re-anchors if the real session is instead observed born directly in working.
The recipe spends real Copilot AI credits on the maintainer's account for the warm-up turn (the slash itself costs nothing). One cheap turn on the auto-routed model (gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5).

model is deliberately NOT pinned in the observation vector: --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks per turn between the two available models, so an exact match would be nondeterministic.

sources.note: CLI 1.0.77 bundle (the binary is a compressed Node SEA, so `strings` yields nothing — this file is the readable source). ~1668868: the /usage command definition returns {kind:"add-timeline-entry"} with no model call. ~7800573: the TUI slash dispatcher returns {handled:true} without entering the prompt path. ~2253182 emitInternal: `u.ephemeral ? … : sessionRecordEventJson(u)` — the persisted/ephemeral split. ~2533038: the SessionEventWriter that is the only writer of events.jsonl. ~8516764 + ~8634781: add-timeline-entry resolves to addEphemeralEntry, in-memory React timeline state. ~8634943: getSessionUsageOutput is a pure read of session logs + quota. ~1625923/~1626175: /clear and /new both call clearHistory (session rotation) — the reason neither is used here.

Only user.message (→ working) and assistant.turn_end (→ turn_done/ready) move state; every other type is Skip, including session.usage_checkpoint via parseUsage (line 301 sets ev.Skip = true). A locally-rendered slash command therefore cannot move state even if it did write a line.

Source = FilesUnderRoot{Dir: $COPILOT_HOME/session-state, SessionIDFromPath} + JSONLineParser: the daemon observes exactly the events.jsonl lines and nothing else, so a UI-only render is invisible by construction.

slash_cmd implements the `slash` step and deliberately does not increment EXPECTED_TURNS (a local render writes no assistant.turn_end); DRIVE_ELICITS includes send/slash/wait_turn/sleep. resolve_transcript resolves on the session DIRECTORY, so it does not block before the warm-up turn creates events.jsonl.
Sibling with the same shape (a slash that appends zero transcript lines): warm-up turn first, then a slash_window phase pinning ready with the two no-transition invariants. Templated from it.

preconditions: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — the warm-up turn spends them; the slash itself costs nothing
irrlichd is recording — run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a daemon started with --record
no other copilot session shares the same cwd (the PID is bound by cwd)

/usage must remain a LOCAL render in the running copilot version — its execute returns {kind:"add-timeline-entry"} with no model call (app.js ~1668868). If a future release routes it through the model, the scenario premise breaks.
setup: The driver seeds a scratch COPILOT_HOME under the staging dir with trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals pre-answered, so the trust modal cannot block the input box; the session directory is minted under $COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/

The warm-up turn goes FIRST and is mandatory: copilot creates the session directory at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only once the first prompt lands, so without it there is no real session for the slash window to be asserted against — only the transient proc-<PID> row

Avoid /clear and /new (both call clearHistory and rotate the session id — session-reset scenario), /compact (a real model call) and a bare /model (opens a picker dialog that would need a keys step to dismiss)

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: warm

verify: events.jsonl mints a proc-<PID> pre-session in ready shortly after launch, then the real <session-id> session under a DIFFERENT id once events.jsonl appears on the warm-up prompt
events.jsonl shows EXACTLY ONE ready→working→ready cycle for the entire run, driven by the warm-up turn only (user.message → working, assistant.turn_end → ready)
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to working after the warm-up turn returns to ready — /usage renders into the UI timeline and appends nothing to the transcript
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting at any point (a local render raises no permission prompt)
the slash window (≥5s after the warm-up turn ends) shows the real session continuously ready
the session's events.jsonl gains no user.message and no assistant.turn_start/turn_end for the /usage invocation
final state of the real session is ready
recipe.notes: Copilot's shape matches codex, not claudecode: the slash command writes NOTHING to the transcript (the TUI dispatcher handles it and returns {handled:true} without ever entering the prompt path that emits user.message), so there is no <local-command> wrapper for the parser to filter — the daemon simply sees no activity. /usage is the chosen command because it renders inline (add-timeline-entry), takes no argument and opens no dialog. What differs between runs: the warm-up reply wording, token counts, session id, PID, timestamps and the AI-credit figures /usage prints. What must NOT differ: a single working arc on the real session, the flat ready slash window, zero tool calls and no waiting.
